description: A sample and hold or track and hold with its own noise source, a chance of skipping the sample, and scale and offset on the output

params.text: Chooses whether a trigger takes one sample and holds it, or the input passes through for as long as the gate is high
Sets the chance that an incoming trigger takes a sample at all, 0% to 100%
Scales the held voltage before it leaves, -100% to +100%
Adds a fixed voltage to the held value, -10V to +10V

inputs.text: Takes a sample on each rising edge in Sample & Hold, or opens the track for as long as it is high in Track & Hold
Shifts the chance of sampling, a tenth of its voltage scaled by the trimpot beside it and added to the PROB knob
Shifts the output scaling, a tenth of its voltage scaled by the trimpot above it and added to the SCL knob
Shifts the output offset, one volt per volt scaled by the trimpot above it and added to the OFS knob
The signal to be sampled; with nothing patched a ±5V noise source is sampled instead

outputs.text: The held voltage, scaled and offset, clamped to ±10V
A 1ms pulse each time a sample is actually taken, or a gate while tracking with 'Gate Out instead Trig' ticked

notes: with the IN jack empty the module samples its own white noise, which is how it doubles as a random voltage source.
a monophonic cable at TRIG samples every channel of a polyphonic IN at once; a polyphonic cable at TRIG samples each channel on its own trigger.
menu: Full — makes the built-in noise an even spread of random voltages between -5V and +5V
Centered — weights the built-in noise towards the middle, and it can step outside ±5V now and then
Sample on HIGH Gate — turns Track & Hold round, so the signal passes while the gate is low and is held while it is high
Trig on start — sends a pulse from the TRIG output when tracking begins
Trig on end — sends a pulse from the TRIG output when tracking ends
Gate Out instead Trig — holds the TRIG output high while tracking instead of pulsing
Noise Generator preset — sets Track & Hold, Sample on HIGH Gate, scale at 100% and offset at 0V in one click, which turns the module into a plain white noise source

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
